items.title: Leon Rene Interview, 1979-05-07
items.q: The interviewee does not mention James B. Johnson directly; the name is only brought up by the interviewer in the context of Bob Wilber playing his numbers.

ctx.x: Not giving the credit to writers whenever they can for that purpose. I think it's a good thing that could be started. I'm going to write a few things on it.

Well, I'll tell you, Bob Wilber's in town. Do you know him by name? He plays soprano and clarinet, and he studied with Bechet. Yeah. And he always, it seems to me, wants to give credit. He wants to do some of James B. Johnson's numbers. Yeah. He's coming up Wednesday. Is that so? He's playing at the Hyatt, you ought to hear him. Is that so? He's gone beyond copying Bechet or Hodges or anything like that. Oh, yeah, so. He's playing Milt Hinton's own bass. Anyway. Is that so? I'm going to ask. Just for a piece of…
That's right. Yeah. And it is their whole survival. I mean, survival of jazz, at least the making of it.
